tess (sec): quick heads up — we're kicking off an RBAC & isolation sweep for the next private deploy wave. goal: ensure least-privilege + auditable KMS flows + minimal egress. thoughts?

omar (infra): +1. can you scope what "sweep" means here? specific services?

tess (sec): mainly: private control plane, edge agents, keystore proxies. also the bastion/jump workflows that ops still uses.

li-wei (platform): need to be careful with the keystore proxy: some tenants use HSM-backed keys with pass-through decryption. we should validate forward secrecy and that logs never capture plaintext.

sanjay (ops): for jump workflows we should push ephemeral certificates via our CA instead of long-lived svc account keys. reduces blast radius.

omar (infra): agree. also propose default NetworkPolicy template: deny all ingress/egress, allow only: dns, ntp, internal-mgmt, and egress to our proxy on 10.0.7.20:3128. I'll paste a quick YAML we can iterate on:

ops-bot: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: np-default-deny-restricted-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.7.20/32
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 3128
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16 # internal mgmt
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

li-wei (platform): that looks good as a start. add a rule to allow access to our KMS endpoint (in private account) on 10.1.1.10:443. and explicitly deny metadata server access from non-bastion pods.

omar (infra): noted. two operational questions: 1) how do we handle audit logs for decrypt operations? 2) can we simulate a KMS outage to validate fallbacks?

tess (sec): 1) audit: we must log only anonymized operation metadata (who requested, key-id, operation type, success/failure, nonce) but never key material. add structured fields to logs for downstream SIEM. sample event: `{actor:sasha, key_id:rk-1234, op:Decrypt, result:FAIL, reason:quota}`. 2) simulate: yes — create a canary that flips to local-derived key fallback and verify audit shows the fallback event and alerting triggers.

sanjay (ops): on (2) we need a safe test harness. propose: deploy a blue/green canary in a non-prod VPC with identical netpols but a mocked KMS that returns controlled errors. then run chaos tests: 503s, latency spikes, and timeouts.

li-wei (platform): for RBAC changes: implement a migration window where we add the new tighter roles as "opt-in" and run an audit report for two weeks to catch missing perms. then switch to enforced mode. We have an audit query in the console: `SELECT event, actor, resource FROM audit_logs WHERE resource LIKE '%keystore%' AND ts > now() - interval '14 days'`

omar (infra): FYI we caught a vuln pattern in the last triage: edge-agent would retry decryption without backoff, revealing KMS endpoint timing differences. fix: exponential backoff + jitter + uniform error responses.

tess (sec): good catch — add that to the playbook under "denial-amplification". also add a checklist item: "ensure error messages to callers are sanitized, avoid leaking if fallback used".

ops-bot: Incident drill reminder: weekly simulated outage scheduled friday 02:00 UTC.

sanjay (ops): aside: how do we want to handle audit retention for private deployments? longer retention for enterprise customers? encryption at rest for logs?

tess (sec): retention policy: default 90 days in the cluster, 1 year in central SIEM for paying customers. all logs encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK) when in private deployments. document this in the contract addendum.

li-wei (platform): implementation note: ship logs over TLS to the collector on 10.0.9.11:9200, use mTLS with certs rotated monthly. collector will redact `request.body` fields matching `(?i)(pass|key|secret)` before indexing.

omar (infra): small nit: some legacy tenants still call the keystore endpoint directly over HTTP — we should block that at the proxy and fail fast with guidance link.

tess (sec): add to rollout checklist: static analysis + runtime check to detect plaintext keystore calls. If found, create a prioritized ticket and don't allow promote to prod until fixed.

sanjay (ops): for onprem installs, customers sometimes request direct HSM access. we should produce a hardened integration guide: network diagrams, firewall rules, HSM endpoint validation steps, and an attestation checklist.

li-wei (platform): I'll draft the integration guide. question: do we allow direct HSM mount into our runtime namespace or only via the keystore proxy?

tess (sec): only via keystore proxy. direct mounts increase host-attack surface. exceptions need a written risk acceptance + SOC signoff.

omar (infra): next steps: i'll open a PR with the networkpolicy template + helm value toggles for KMS endpoints and proxy IP. li-wei will add RBAC migration plan. tess will update playbook + audit schema. sanjay will prepare canary harness.

tess (sec): thanks team — please tag me on PRs and add checklist items to the private-deploy runbook. we'll schedule a 30m sync after PRs land. :thumbsup:
